record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Find a minimum-size family of positive circles whose vertex sets cover all vertices of a signed graph Σ.

evidence.quote: C1–4. Like P4.1–4.1 but for the minimum number, or minimum sets, of negative (or positive) circles that cover all the vertices of Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph Σ = (G, σ) consists of a finite (multi)graph G = (V, E) together with a sign function σ : E → {+1, −1}. The sign of a circle (i.e., a simple cycle) C in Σ is the product of the signs of its edges; C is called positive if this product is +1 and negative otherwise. The vertex set of a circle C is the set of vertices appearing on C.

A family F = {C_1, C_2, …, C_k} of positive circles in Σ is said to vertex-cover Σ if every vertex of Σ lies on at least one circle C_i ∈ F (vertices not lying on any positive circle make a vertex-cover by positive circles impossible, so assume Σ admits such a covering).

Problem. Determine, for an arbitrary signed graph Σ that admits a vertex-cover by positive circles, the minimum cardinality
   π_+(Σ) := min { |F| : F is a family of positive circles whose vertex sets cover V(Σ) },
and characterize the families F achieving this minimum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative and positive circles in signed graphs (published 2018 in AKCE Int. J. Graphs Combin.). Web search indicates these vertex-covering questions for positive/negative circles are listed as unresolved with no published solutions located.
